<Picture 1> is the AUTHORITATIVE NAVIGATION MAP of this ride, north up: a top-down map of a Yuanmingyuan-style imperial garden park with the ride route drawn as a thin dark LINE from the west end of the lake causeway ('start') east along the causeway to the junction plaza ('turn'), then a RIGHT turn SOUTH along the lakeside path to a lakeside terrace ('end'). Blue = lotus lake, grey = stone paths, green dots = trees, black blocks = red-walled imperial halls. The map is a flat planning legend only; it must NEVER appear inside the video world - no red lines, dots, markers, text or rings painted anywhere; real paths are plain grey stone.

The REFERENCE VIDEO is the last few seconds of the ride so far: your exact current position, heading, speed and view. This clip MUST continue seamlessly from the END of that reference video - the identical place, heading and handlebar view, moving forward at the same speed without any hesitation or repositioning.

FIRST-PERSON BICYCLE CAMERA, non-negotiable: handlebar-mounted camera at exactly 1.6 meters, looking straight ahead horizontally; the handlebar grips and both rider's hands are ALWAYS VISIBLE at the bottom edge of every frame; ground fills the lower half; horizon near the middle; camera NEVER rises; NO aerial/drone/bird's-eye/top-down view.

ONE CONTINUOUS RIDE, no stopping, no slowing (total 10.0 seconds at 24 fps). This clip covers the SECOND half of map leg L1: keep riding EAST along the narrow stone causeway exactly as in your current view, white marble balustrades on both sides, lotus lake water on BOTH sides; the junction plaza W1 (the grey circle on the map where the causeway meets the north-south path) grows ahead - a broad stone-paved square shaded by a big tree, with red-walled imperial halls standing near its corners; the clip CUTS just as you glide INTO the plaza square at full cruise speed - do NOT turn yet, do NOT slow down, no cuts inside the clip.
